messages:
ashley: Heads up — main CI went red right after I pushed a lock regen + venv upgrade for my WIP. Failing a couple of tests (kvcache + grpc integ). I can repro inside the docker image. Anyone free for a quick bisect?

sam: Can you paste the CI link and a short log snippet? pinging @tess in case it's a transitive dep bump :eyes:

ashley: CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/1763 — failing job on ubuntu-latest. Log snippet:
```
FAILED tests/test_kvcache.py::test_cache_eviction - AssertionError: expected 'x' == 'y'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"tests/test_kvcache.py\", line 42, in test_cache_eviction
    assert cache.get(k) == v
```

Also ran `docker build` + `tox -e py39` and got same failure locally.

tess: That looks like a parsing/encoding regression. Did `poetry lock` bump anything like rfc3986/httpcore/urllib3? Can you paste the lock diff (or `git show` for the lock commit)?

ashley: Pasted the lock diff in the branch: shows `rfc3986 1.4.0 -> 2.0.1` and `httpcore 0.16.0 -> 0.17.0`. Minimal local test: installing `rfc3986==1.4.0` makes the failing test pass.

marc: If pinning rfc3986 fixes it locally then it's probably downstream pulling a major bump. Quick workaround is an explicit constraint in pyproject. Long-term we need to figure out which package pulled it.

sam: I can run a quick bisect on the lockfile automation to see which dependency forced the bump. @ashley can you point me to the regen commit?

ashley: Branch `ashley/lock-regen-2026` — commit `b3f8d2` is the lock regen. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/commit/b3f8d2

ci-bot: New build triggered by @sam for branch ashley/lock-regen-2026 — https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/1764

sam: Bisect results: culprit = `azure-core` bump in our constraints; it pulled `msal` which pulled `rfc3986>=2.0`. Repro command I used:
```
# bisect script (local)
git checkout b3f8d2~2..b3f8d2 -- poetry.lock
for c in $(git rev-list --reverse b3f8d2~2..b3f8d2); do git checkout $c -- poetry.lock && poetry install -n && pytest tests/test_kvcache.py::test_cache_eviction || echo "bad $c"; done
```
Found the exact step where rfc3986 jumped.

tess: OK — short-term patch: add `rfc3986 = \"==1.4.0\"` to the `[tool.poetry.dev-dependencies]` (or main deps) to keep CI stable. We should also open an issue to track updating our code for rfc3986 2.x behaviors.

ashley: I pushed a quick PR that pins `rfc3986` and adds a changelog note: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234. Can someone review + approve?

jordan: Quick review now — LGTM, small commit message nit (use imperative tense).

sam: Approving and will merge once CI passes the rerun. Rerunning the affected job now.

ci-bot: Rerun complete for PR 1234 — status: success (all checks green).

ashley: Awesome, thanks everyone! :tada: I'll follow up with an issue to track the azure-core/msal chain and schedule a constraints sweep.

marc: Thumbs up. Also add a note to the next infra retro so we can decide how to handle major transitive bumps in future.

sam: Filed issue #456 to track and assigned to @tess for triage.

ashley: Thanks all. Closing this thread.
